items.title: Binance Hack Lessons: Sandbox the Take-Home Assignment
items.summary: A fake take-home assignment replaced a Homebrew binary on a Binance work laptop. SafeDep rebuilt that setup step as a benign lab and ran it with and without the pmg sandbox. The post gives the commands, the real output and the limits of the sandbox.

items.title: Binance Hack: How Attackers Stole $6.34 Billion Through Developer Laptops
items.summary: The October 29, 2026 Binance hack started on developer laptops. A tampered Homebrew install and a fake job interview gave a North Korean group its first access. A short breakdown of the attack path.

items.title: antd-img-crop GitHub Repository Hijacked to Deliver OverLord Stealer
items.summary: A forged commit force-pushed to the antd-img-crop GitHub repository runs a dropper on npm run build that installs a cross-platform stealer and remote-access agent called OverLord. The npm package is clean.

items.title: October 2026 Security Incident Review: PHP, Binance, Cursor, LiteLLM and More
items.summary: October was Cybersecurity Awareness Month. It was also the month PHP, Railway, OpenCode, Binance, Polymarket, Cursor, LiteLLM and eight more made the news for a security incident. A short recap of what happened to each one.

items.title: testmetest npm Packages Carry a Miasma-Family Worm
items.summary: 19 npm packages carry a Miasma-family worm that steals credentials, spreads to other packages and installs a wiper. The newest builds start the worm when an application loads the package.

items.title: eMudhra CA Key Compromise: Response Guide for Developers
items.summary: Anyone can compute eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys from public certificates. Browsers block the compromised intermediates, but CI runners, containers, JVMs and Go binaries can still trust forged certificates. Test and update affected systems, and decide whether to rotate credentials.

items.title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
items.summary: Every wheel of LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI installs a credential stealer and a remote code execution backdoor. Both run each time Python starts. The code is not in the upstream GitHub source.

items.title: Forged Commits Push a preinstall Dropper into hugo-paper and mevn-cli
items.summary: An attacker pushed forged commits to the default branches of hugo-paper and mevn-cli. Running npm install or bun install in either repository downloads and runs a second-stage script from buildwithknexus[.]xyz.

items.title: MALFEX Moves Its npm Loader into a Native Windows DLL
items.summary: The MALFEX package imgdecode contains a native Windows loader. When loaded from a console, it attempts to download, decrypt, and inject shellcode into dllhost.exe.

items.title: ASOS App Hack: Attackers Used Push Notifications to Send a Ransom Note
items.summary: Attackers got into the platforms ASOS uses to message customers and pushed an extortion note to phones. Here is what is confirmed, what is only claimed, and what customers should do.

items.title: tensorlake 0.5.144 npm Compromise Ships Mini Shai-Hulud
items.summary: tensorlake@0.5.144 on npm ran a Mini Shai-Hulud worm at install. A maintainer account committed the payload through the GitHub web interface, and the official release workflow published it.

items.title: 42 Malicious RubyGems Open a Reverse Shell at Install Time
items.summary: One RubyGems account published 42 gems that run code during gem install. On a developer workstation, the gems open a reverse shell or download a second stage. They do nothing on CI runners and sandboxes.

items.title: An Attacker Hijacked an AI Coding Assistant to Spread a Worm
items.summary: An attacker took over a live AI coding assistant session, got it to recommend a poisoned package, and used the stolen tokens to spread the Shai-Hulud worm across about 100 internal repositories.

items.title: PolinRider Switches to Ethereum C2 in 30+ Repositories
items.summary: A malicious pull request against oxc led SafeDep to a larger campaign. The PolinRider loader family now reads its C2 servers from Ethereum transactions. SafeDep confirmed 35 GitHub repositories that still carry the loader, two operator wallets, and 11 C2 servers.

items.title: DirtyBlanket: Fake Express Packages on npm Spread a Linux Worm
items.summary: Nine fake Express and React packages on npm run a Linux worm at install time. It installs a Tor backdoor and spreads through SSH, AUR packages, and npm tokens.

items.title: Detecting Compromised AI Coding Agents with Jev and Gryph
items.summary: I checked every action of my own Claude Code agent against a profile of how I work and a set of org policies, using Jev. It caught 14 of 14 attacks for $0.15 per 1,000 events.

items.title: Mini Shai-Hulud Is Still Infecting GitHub Repositories
items.summary: The May 2026 Mini Shai-Hulud worm is still infecting new GitHub repositories. Hijacked actions-cool/issues-helper tags planted Claude Code and VS Code hooks in six popular repositories between 20 and 24 September.

items.title: MemTensor npm and PyPI Packages Hit by a Go Worm
items.summary: An attacker used a Go worm to steal CI publish tokens from MemTensor and ship malicious MemOS packages to npm and PyPI. See how it works, with code and indicators of compromise.

items.title: sckit: A New Go Implant Framework for Supply Chain Worms
items.summary: sckit is a Go implant framework that steals developer and CI credentials and carries templates to spread through npm, PyPI, and GitHub Actions. Static analysis and indicators of compromise.

items.title: OpenAI Agents Turned RubyGems Into a Scraping Proxy
items.summary: Between May and July 2026, a swarm of AI agents published over 3,000 packages to RubyGems. The gems abused RubyDoc.info documentation builds to run a crawler on someone else's servers, then shipped the scraped data back to the registry as new gems and webhook URLs. Three independent researchers traced the campaign to OpenAI agents four months later.
